subject: Realtime output stall: persistent WebSocket chunk hang impacting Cardinal Health (urgent)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalhealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.desai@cardinalhealth.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime endpoint stall observed in production

Team —

We're seeing a production issue that started ~07:30 PT this morning and has been intermittent but severe: roughly 20–30% of websocket streaming requests to the /v1/realtime/ws route are establishing a connection and receiving the first chunk, then hanging (no additional chunks) for >30s before timing out on our side. When the stall happens the client eventually reconnects and the subsequent request works; no consistent payload boundary or prompt appears to correlate.

Impact: our order-processing pipeline backs up (we're seeing 8–12 minute tail latencies for downstream workers) and our SLO alerts are firing. We collected traces and a sample tcpdump; attaching websocket-trace-20261120.zip and a small prod_error_snippet.txt with the last few HTTP frames.

Questions:
- Is this a known issue with chunked transfer handling on the new runtime?
- Any immediate mitigations you recommend (keepalives, shorter timeouts, non-streaming fallback)?

We need an ETA to fix or a reliable mitigation — this is now blocking customer-facing SLAs.

— Liam
Product Ops, Cardinal Health AI Labs

---

(attachment: websocket-trace-20261120.zip, prod_error_snippet.txt)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalhealth.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime endpoint stall observed in production

Liam — thanks for the clear summary and the traces. Sorry for the impact here. I'm escalating to engineering and CS; I've copied Laura and Sean.

Immediate plan (MAP):
1) Sean & eng to triage logs and confirm whether this is a runtime chunking regression (target: 2 hrs)
2) Short-term mitigation: switch the affected calls to our non-streaming /v1/complete endpoint or enable explicit keepalive pings on the websocket (we can advise client config).
3) If mitigation unacceptable, we'll provision a temporary dedicated routing rule for your traffic to a conservative kernel profile that disables the fast-chunk batching (takes ~30m).
4) We'll provide hourly status updates until resolved.

Could you also confirm: which reverse proxy are you using in front of your workers (Envoy/ALB/other) and whether you have an L4 TCP proxy that might be closing idle streams? The traces point at a clean first-chunk then silence — could be either our runtime or an infra-level proxy drop.

I've attached a one-page MAP (MAP_Cardinal_20261120.pdf). I'll set up a 30-min war room if needed.

— Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(attachment: MAP_Cardinal_20261120.pdf)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime endpoint stall observed in production — initial triage

Looping in initial findings so everyone's on the same page.

Notes from quick triage of the provided traces:
- The runtime sent the first SSE/chunk payload and did not emit further application-level frames for ~32s in the example trace.
- Our server-side logs show the generator produced tokens but the chunk-flusher thread did not commit the next chunk until a wakeup event — this looks like interaction between the kernel batching logic and the socket write path under certain MTU/proxy combinations.
- Probable repro vector: combination of Nagle-ish coalescing on the customer side + an intermediary L7 proxy that buffers until it sees a larger chunk.

Immediate ask from Cardinal: please try one of the following and report results:
1) Reproduce the same request but add periodic websocket pings from client to keep the TCP stream active (we frequently see proxies flush on activity).
2) Route one test request through an alternate path (no proxy) to see if problem goes away.
3) Capture a tcpdump at the earliest hop in your infra and share (we need to see the ACK/PSH timing).

We opened Jira RDW-8273 to track the runtime-side hypothesis; I'll attach debug flags on our side and run an instrumented deploy to one of your test routes. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890.

If these reproductions show the proxy as the cause we will walk Cardinal through recommended proxy config. If it's on our side we'll prioritize a patch — Sean (eng lead) will coordinate.

— Sean
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

(Referenced: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RDW-8273)

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@cardinalhealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@cardinalhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime endpoint stall observed in production — impact update

Karthik / Sean —

We tried the non-streaming fallback you suggested (POST /v1/complete) and it works consistently, but it doubles average latency for the flows that rely on progressive decoding. That doubling breaks downstream SLA windows and isn't viable for high-throughput order ingest.

We also tried adding websocket pings; that reduced the incidence but did not eliminate stalls (we still saw ~5% of requests hang). This is a production-impact issue and our CRO has asked us to escalate for executive attention and a commitment on ETA / credits for SLA breaches.

Below is the snippet our infra team forwarded last night: (forwarded)

Summary:
- Impact: order pipeline tail latency is spiking; customer saw up to ~30% initial stall rate, now reduced to ~5% with temporary client-side keepalive.
- Current state: Jira RDW-8273 opened; Sean has an instrumented deploy scheduled and is triaging kernel-level chunk flush behavior.
